form.modelNameDescription: The name of the model. This will be used to reference the model in the API. You can track price changes of models by using the same name and match pattern.

form.startDateDescription: If set, the model will only be used for generations after this date.
form.unitDescription: The unit of measurement for the model.
form.tokenizerDescription: Optionally, Deeptrace can tokenize the input and output of a generation if no unit counts are ingested. This is useful for e.g. streamed OpenAI completions.
form.tokenizerConfigDescription: The config for the tokenizer. Required for openai.
form.Enter total price: Enter total price only if no separate input and output prices are provided.

config.modelName: Standardized model name. Generations are assigned to this model name if they match the `matchPattern` upon ingestion.
config.matchPattern: Regex pattern to match `model` parameter of generations to model pricing
config.startDate: Date to start pricing model. If not set, model is active unless a more recent version exists.
config.inputPrice: Price per one million units of input
config.outputPrice: Price per one million units of output
config.totalPrice: Price per one million units, for models that don't have input/output specific prices
config.unit: Unit of measurement for generative model, can be TOKENS, CHARACTERS, SECONDS, MILLISECONDS, REQUESTS or IMAGES.
config.tokenizerId: Tokenizer used for this model to calculate token counts if none are ingested. Pick from list of supported tokenizers.
config.config: Some tokenizers require additional configuration (e.g. openai tiktoken). See docs for details.

tooltips.temperature: The sampling temperature. Higher values will make the output more random, while lower values will make it more focused and deterministic.
tooltips.outputTokenLimit: The maximum number of tokens that can be generated in the chat completion.
tooltips.topP: An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or temperature but not both.
